EDGE-pos1.label: violation
EDGE-pos1.note: The sensor lease port adds a method that returns the raw vendor lease, typed with an inline import('hivepulse-sdk') type.

EDGE-pos2.label: violation
EDGE-pos2.note: The outbound ports index publishes the lease gateway adapter with export *, and the composition root takes the gateway from there.

EDGE-pos3.label: violation
EDGE-pos3.note: The lease gateway moves to src/domain/sensors/; the spec puts that folder in the domain layer, and the file imports the SDK.

EDGE-twin1.label: clean
EDGE-twin1.note: The webhook DTO types the colony state with an inline import('hivepulse-sdk') type; an inbound adapter may depend on the vendor's types.

EDGE-twin2.label: clean
EDGE-twin2.note: The telemetry webhook moves to src/webhooks/ and checks the vendor signature with the SDK; the spec adds src/webhooks/** to the inbound adapter layer.

FIELD-pos1.label: violation
FIELD-pos1.note: The domain reads a raw frame through a table keyed by the vendor's field names, and the telemetry use case applies it to the frame the port carries.

FIELD-pos2.label: violation
FIELD-pos2.note: The core colony reading declares the vendor's weight_kg field under the vendor's name, carried from the frame through the port.

FIELD-twin1.label: clean
FIELD-twin1.note: The placement keeps the grower's pollination contract, whose snake_case field names are the apiary's own contract form fields, declared in the spec glossary.

FIELD-twin2.label: clean
FIELD-twin2.note: The core colony reading keeps the hive weight under the domain's own name, hiveMassKg; the webhook handler maps weight_kg to it.

KEY-pos1.label: violation
KEY-pos1.note: The telemetry use case derives the vigour with an equality chain over the vendor's colony states, with the state text the port carries.

KEY-pos2.label: violation
KEY-pos2.note: The domain decides whether sensors are live from a Map keyed by the vendor's lease states, read with the state text the lease port carries.

KEY-twin1.label: clean
KEY-twin1.note: The delivery rule scores colonies from a Record keyed by the core's own vigour words.

KEY-twin2.label: clean
KEY-twin2.note: The webhook handler replaces its switch with a Map keyed by the vendor's colony states; the lookup stays in the inbound adapter.

RULE-pos1.label: violation
RULE-pos1.note: The lease gateway decides how many sensors a yard gets (one per four hives, at least two); the use case passes the hive count and the domain no longer holds the promise.

RULE-pos2.label: violation
RULE-pos2.note: The webhook handler downgrades a colony to weak when its brood is below 33 degrees, the apiary's health rule; the domain has no such rule.

RULE-twin1.label: clean
RULE-twin1.note: The webhook handler drops a frame it has already seen (same hive tag and timestamp), since the vendor retries deliveries; technical work only.

RULE-twin2.label: clean
RULE-twin2.note: Same feature as the brood temperature rule, but the domain holds it: the handler passes the temperature and the delivery rule downgrades cold colonies.

SET-pos1.label: violation
SET-pos1.note: The domain declares an enum copy of the vendor's six colony states, and the telemetry use case casts the state text the port carries to it.

SET-pos2.label: violation
SET-pos2.note: The domain declares a const array copy of the vendor's lease states; the lease port carries the vendor's state text and the use case casts it.

SET-twin1.label: clean
SET-twin1.note: The domain declares its own sensor coverage words; the lease gateway maps the vendor's lease state and unit count to them.

SET-twin2.label: clean
SET-twin2.note: The domain declares the outcomes of an on-site inspection; nominal is the only word it shares with the vendor's six colony states, and the glossary declares the set as ours.

WORD-pos1.label: violation
WORD-pos1.note: The colony reading gains the sensor's firmware under the vendor's field name, carried from the telemetry frame through the port.

WORD-pos2.label: violation
WORD-pos2.note: The colony vigour gains the vendor's absconded colony state word as a core value.

WORD-twin1.label: clean
WORD-twin1.note: The apiary's own hive inspection marks a colony queenless and the placement keeps it; the spec glossary declares queenless as a domain term.

WORD-twin2.label: clean
WORD-twin2.note: The placement keeps the timestamp of the last on-site inspection, sent over HTTP; timestamp is a generic word the vendor also uses as a field.
